observations.observed: R1 uses the vague phrase 「必要な placeholder」 without defining which option kinds require one or what concrete placeholder contract applies.
R6 requires E2E verification using 「代表ケース」 but does not define the selection or coverage criteria for a representative case.
The subjective term 「代表ケース」 leaves the required E2E coverage unspecified, so independent reviewers cannot agree on whether the verification scope is sufficient.
The acceptance criterion refers to 「representative docs/core/plugin group help」 without identifying the required surfaces or a measurable representativeness rule.
T-6 acceptance requires 「代表的な docs/core/plugin group help」 but does not define which examples must be covered or how selection is judged.
T-7 acceptance refers to 「代表的な接続シナリオ」 without defining the scenarios that are mandatory or the selection criterion.
T-7 acceptance requires checking 「必要な結果」 but does not identify which results are required at each test layer.

R3 explicitly permits recording 「size/retry/context limit または上限なし」. Retry and resource-related processing therefore have no required upper bound, contrary to the guardrail's prohibition on unbounded processing.
T-4 repeats the allowance 「size/retry/context limit または上限なし」, so the planned inventory can accept unbounded retry or resource processing instead of requiring explicit limits.

The spec does not list the concrete user-facing argument set with each argument's type, format, and range. It defers deriving a test-only inventory from the live registry and owners, while only naming categories and examples; internal arguments are not provided as a complete marked inventory either.

The spec gives category-level exit codes for valid help/success, parser/target/command failures, and no-leaf help, but does not state success and failure conditions for each modified command or leaf individually.
